_meta.description: Risk-level escalation rules and shared clinical rationale text for the Day 5 Recommender agent. Per-diagnosis baseline tests/treatments live in conditions.json; this file layers risk-level and age adjustments on top.

treatments: Further diagnostic workup to establish diagnosis

additional_tests: Continuous cardiac and vital sign monitoring

follow_up_by_risk_level.LOW: Follow up in 1-2 weeks if symptoms are not improving.
follow_up_by_risk_level.MEDIUM: Recheck labs and symptoms within 48 hours.

test_rationale.Chest X-ray: Confirms diagnosis and assesses severity or extent
test_rationale.Blood culture: Identifies the causative organism to guide targeted antibiotic therapy
test_rationale.CBC: Assesses infection, inflammation, or anemia severity via blood cell counts
test_rationale.Basic metabolic panel: Checks kidney function and electrolyte balance
test_rationale.Sputum culture: Identifies the causative organism in the airway
test_rationale.Rapid influenza test: Confirms influenza to guide antiviral treatment timing
test_rationale.Rapid strep test: Rules out bacterial (strep) cause of sore throat
test_rationale.Vital signs monitoring: Tracks basic physiological stability over time
test_rationale.Spirometry: Assesses lung function and degree of airway obstruction
test_rationale.D-dimer: Screens for clot activity; elevated result raises suspicion for thromboembolism
test_rationale.CT pulmonary angiogram: Directly visualizes pulmonary arteries to confirm or rule out embolism
test_rationale.Chest CT scan: Provides detailed imaging when X-ray findings are inconclusive
test_rationale.Upper endoscopy: Directly visualizes the esophageal lining to assess reflux damage
test_rationale.ECG: Detects heart rhythm abnormalities and ischemic changes
test_rationale.Troponin: Detects myocardial injury indicating a possible heart attack
test_rationale.Echocardiogram: Assesses heart structure, function, and surrounding fluid
test_rationale.Coronary angiography: Directly visualizes coronary arteries to locate blockages
test_rationale.Stress test: Evaluates heart function under exertion to detect reduced blood flow
test_rationale.Cardiac monitoring: Continuously tracks heart rhythm to catch arrhythmias
test_rationale.Iron studies: Determines the cause and severity of anemia
test_rationale.Blood glucose test: Rules out hypoglycemia as a cause of symptoms
test_rationale.Thyroid function tests: Rules out thyroid dysfunction as a cause of palpitations or rhythm changes
test_rationale.Allergy testing (post-recovery): Identifies the specific allergen trigger once the patient is stable
test_rationale.Continuous pulse oximetry: Detects early respiratory deterioration in real time
test_rationale.Repeat labs in 12 hours: Tracks whether the patient is trending toward improvement or decline
test_rationale.Repeat vital signs in 4-6 hours: Confirms the patient remains stable before discharge
test_rationale.Continuous cardiac and vital sign monito: Catches sudden deterioration immediately in a critical patient
test_rationale.Arterial blood gas: Directly measures oxygenation, ventilation, and acid-base status in critical illness
test_rationale.ECG (baseline cardiac assessment): Establishes a cardiac baseline before treatment in older patients
test_rationale.Renal function panel (medication dose ad: Guides safe medication dosing given age-related kidney function decline

treatment_rationale.Antibiotic (amoxicillin or azithromycin): Targets the likely bacterial cause of infection
treatment_rationale.Supportive care: Manages symptoms while the underlying process resolves
treatment_rationale.Rest and fluids: Supports the body's natural recovery process
treatment_rationale.Antiviral medication (if within 48h of o: Reduces severity and duration when started early
treatment_rationale.Bronchodilator (albuterol): Relaxes airway muscles to relieve wheezing and obstruction
treatment_rationale.Anticoagulation therapy: Prevents clot growth and new clot formation
treatment_rationale.Chest tube placement (if large): Re-expands the collapsed lung by removing trapped air
treatment_rationale.Proton pump inhibitor: Reduces stomach acid production to relieve reflux symptoms
treatment_rationale.Aspirin: Reduces further clot formation in acute coronary syndrome
treatment_rationale.Nitroglycerin: Relieves chest pain by dilating coronary arteries
treatment_rationale.Beta-blocker: Reduces the heart's oxygen demand and controls heart rate
treatment_rationale.Emergency reperfusion therapy (PCI): Restores blood flow to the blocked coronary artery
treatment_rationale.Anticoagulant (for AFib): Reduces stroke risk from atrial clot formation
treatment_rationale.Iron supplementation: Replenishes iron stores to correct anemia
treatment_rationale.Blood transfusion (if severe): Rapidly restores oxygen-carrying capacity in severe anemia
treatment_rationale.Anti-anxiety medication (short-term): Provides rapid symptom relief in severe cases
treatment_rationale.Nasal saline irrigation: Clears nasal passages and reduces congestion
treatment_rationale.Epinephrine injection: Reverses a life-threatening allergic reaction immediately
treatment_rationale.IV fluids: Supports blood pressure and organ perfusion
treatment_rationale.Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics: Covers likely pathogens immediately while cultures are pending
treatment_rationale.Vasopressors (if needed): Maintains adequate blood pressure in shock
treatment_rationale.Outpatient management appropriate: Condition is stable enough for home management with routine follow-up
treatment_rationale.Consider short observation period: Allows brief monitoring to confirm the patient is trending toward improvement
treatment_rationale.Hospital admission for close monitoring: Enables rapid response to deterioration that outpatient care can't provide
treatment_rationale.ICU admission: Provides continuous monitoring and immediate intervention capability
treatment_rationale.Immediate stabilization measures: Addresses life-threatening derangements before further workup
treatment_rationale.Further diagnostic workup to establish d: Narrows the differential when no diagnosis is confidently established yet
